q1_issues.issue: (Result sk_cease_1 sk_french_1) inverts the sentence — it says the ceasing produced the state of being French, when the sentence says that state ends.

The french state is reified and asserted positively at top level (with its Experiencer at index 12) with no Past, no strength-0 denial and nothing marking it as the ceased state, so the parse claims the people are French.
The cease event carries only (Patient sk_cease_1 sk_people_1) and no Theme naming the ceased eventuality, unlike the inceptive mirror pattern where Theme is the activity's own witness.
"would cease" is future-in-the-past and the instruction set maps "would V" to Future, but the parse marks it (Past sk_cease_1).
The whole "Once X had ..., Y would ..." conditional is asserted flat as two occurred past events plus a Before ordering, so the parse claims both clauses actually happened.
The two parallel flat copular atoms are treated inconsistently — (Member sk_people_1 indigenous) is bare while the parallel french atom at index 14 is wrapped in Past.

q2_gaps: "Once X had V-ed, Y would V" — a temporal-conditional with a "would" main clause; the instruction set covers indicative if-conditionals as Implication rules, "every time / whenever", and subjunctive counterfactuals, but nothing for this form, and it gives no general treatment of the modal "would" outside an embedded eventuality under a causative verb.

Copular change-of-state verbs ("become / turn / grow" + a predicative complement): the two-kinds-of-clause split has no branch for them, and the resultative section covers only a transitive verb with an object plus a result predicate.

Aspectual "cease / stop" taking a copular complement ("cease to be French"): the cessation section covers only "stopped / quit V-ing" over an activity and the stative "no longer / not anymore / used to" wordings, so ceasing a state named by a predicate adjective has no form.
notes: Every head used is licensed; the failures are in what is asserted, not in vocabulary. The Before ordering between the past perfect and the main clause is itself the right canonical treatment for the temporal connective "once".
